assets.description: A pine marten watching an oak leaf above a mossy book in a forest library.
assets.finalPrompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: original fantasy collectible-card artwork for Spellbook's private user profile, displayed as a small landscape picture.
Scene: a huge old forest library grown into living roots. Close foreground, a wild pine marten familiar with glossy dark eyes and a pale throat patch balances on a closed, weathered moss-green book wedged between roots. It is stretching toward one copper oak leaf suspended over its nose; its long curved tail makes a clean sweeping silhouette. The woodland is a few broad silhouettes and fern fronds, not a wall of detail.
Art direction: professional hand-painted fantasy card illustration, expressive opaque gouache and thin oil glazes on textured board. Confident visible brushwork, sophisticated draftsmanship, natural animal anatomy, selective sharp edges around the face and book, loose quieter edges in the background. Looks like a commissioned painting scanned from an artist's studio, never a 3D render. Strange and endearing without looking like a mascot or children's sticker.
Composition: one landscape image, 3:2 aspect ratio. Intimate low three-quarter view; the marten and book fill the central two thirds, with the face clear near center. Bold light-dark shapes that remain readable at 340x210px. Full bleed painting edge to edge, no framing. Preserve subject away from the outer 10 percent for modest cropping.
Palette and light: deep pine green, olive, ochre parchment and small russet leaf accents. One dappled shaft of warm afternoon sunlight touches the animal's face, restrained natural highlights, rich dark root shadows. Luminous pigment rather than glowing magic.
Constraints: completely original creature and scene, no known fictional characters. No text, letters, writing, symbols, logos, signatures, watermarks, UI, borders or card frame. No photorealism, airbrushing, 3D, cute giant eyes, anime, epic wizard, purple magical haze, flying particles, clutter, bokeh, extreme bloom, generic fantasy wallpaper. Generate one single finished illustration.

assets.description: A silver-haired archivist protecting a book at a sea archive during a storm.

Scene: the open stone doorway of a sea archive during a storm. An older woman archivist in a weathered mustard-yellow oilskin coat stands firmly on wet black steps, turned three-quarter profile into the wind. She holds one closed heavy sea-green volume against her torso with both forearms, its plain cover tied with a cord. Her cropped silver hair and coat hem blow sideways. Behind her, a monumental curling teal wave rolls past the doorway, with a pale gull riding the air above it. Her calm, stubborn expression contrasts with the force of the water. A section of salt-worn shelves just inside the doorway quietly makes the place an archive.

Crisp face, simple substantial coat folds, broad carved-looking wave strokes, quieter background. Looks like a commissioned painting scanned from an artist's studio, no 3D render or photo effect. Strange lived-in fantasy, not cinematic wallpaper.

The creature has the long low body of a real fire salamander, broad blunt head, small intelligent amber eyes, four clearly placed sturdy feet, and overlapping charcoal and burnt-red mineral plates like cooling kiln glaze. It gently rests one front foot on a single unfinished copper ring on the anvil. Warm ember light shines through a few fine cracks between its plates, suggesting a creature that keeps the forge warm. An old pair of tongs leans against stone at the side; no people. Its tail curves around the anvil's foot. Behind is one broad furnace opening with banked coals and warm terracotta masonry, quiet and dim, no roaring flames.

assets.description: A brass armillary sphere framing the moon in a ruined mountain observatory.

Scene: a forgotten open-roof observatory high above a quiet midnight valley. A monumental antique brass armillary sphere sits on a low blue stone pedestal in the foreground, its few broad interlocking orbital rings framing a pale waxing moon in the real sky beyond. The mechanism has believable rivets and tarnished edges, and a small smooth ivory globe at its center. A worn closed indigo book rests on the pedestal. Through a broken circular observatory aperture behind it, see a few distant slate mountains and a deep blue night sky with sparse tiny natural stars. No people or animals. The sphere, moon and architectural arch make an elegant, unusual alignment, like a quiet discovery rather than a spectacle.
Art direction: professional hand-painted fantasy collectible-card illustration. Opaque gouache and oil glazes on textured board, rich layered blue pigments, visible assured brushwork, deliberate edge control, convincing metal geometry and weathered stone. Crisp restrained highlights on brass, broad quiet background strokes. A commissioned studio painting scanned from textured board, not a photograph or 3D render. Scholarly celestial mystery without purple magical clouds.

Low three-quarter close view of the large brass instrument; concentric ring silhouette dominant in central two thirds, with the moon visible cleanly within the open rings. A few simple strong shapes, readable instantly at 340x210px. Main instrument, book and moon inside central 80 percent. Rings are solid engineered metal bands, coherent perspective and intersections, no tangled wire.
